title: Probe-driven degradation scoring and derate policy for autoscaler stability
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Current readiness/liveness probe signals are binary and siloed per-region. During partial degradations we see rapid autoscaler oscillation (thrashing) and aggressive cross-region failovers that breach SLOs. We also lack a consistent mechanism to convert multiple probe failures + degraded latency into a single, tunable derate signal for the autoscaler and circuit breakers.\n\nGoal: Implement a probe-driven degradation scoring system that: (1) ingests per-instance readiness/liveness, latency percentiles, and error-rate signals; (2) computes a weighted continuous degradation score per endpoint and per region; (3) exposes the score to autoscaler controllers and circuit-breaker policies so they can perform derated scaling and staged failover instead of aggressive binary actions. The solution should reduce autoscaler oscillation, improve multi-region failover stability, and keep SLO breach risk low during noisy signals.
acceptance_criteria: Derivation: A documented scoring function (weights and decay windows) exists and is stored in repo as code and a human-readable spec.
Metrics: In staging, introducing the scoring input reduces autoscaler scale-up/scale-down rate by >=40% during synthetic noise tests while keeping 95th latency within SLO 99% of time.
Rollout controls: Canary config is available to enable scoring for single route in one region and a toggle for circuit-breaker integration.
Observability: New dashboards show degradation score, contributing signals, autoscaler decisions, and failover actions per region.
Fail-safe: If scoring service is unavailable, system falls back to current binary probe behavior and emits alert.
work_plan: Design scoring model: define input signals (readiness, liveness, p50/p95 latency, error-rate, instance load) and weight/decay policy.
Prototype service: lightweight scoring microservice that subscribes to health-stream and exposes per-route/region score via gRPC + metrics endpoint.
Controller integration: update autoscaler controller to accept a 'derate_factor' derived from score and to apply damped scaling (rate-limited, hysteresis).
Circuit-breaker update: allow graded thresholds driven by score (soft-open -> hard-open) and staged traffic steering to secondary region.
Testing: chaos/stress tests in staging with synthetic probe failures, latency spikes, and partial region degradations.
Observability: add dashboards and alerts; define SLO guardrails and playbook entries for on-call.
Canary & rollout: enable per-route canary, monitor, gradually expand to production regions, post-mortem after rollout.
risks: Scoring mis-calibration could mask real failures and delay necessary scale-up leading to SLO violations.
Additional latency/complexity from scoring service introduces a new dependency; must avoid single-point-of-failure.
Controller changes add complexity; improper hysteresis tuning can still cause slow response to real demand surges.
Cross-region topologies make failover behavior subtle; policy must avoid cascading reroutes under transient noise.
mitigations: Start with conservative weights and short, opt-in canaries for low-traffic routes.
Run scoring service in-mesh with redundancy and instrument a critical-path fallback to binary probes.
Implement safety caps: max derate percentage and maximum rate-limit for scale-up for first 5 minutes after derate change.
Add automated rollback if combined SLO indicators (error budget burn, p95 latency) cross thresholds during canary.
notes: We will use Exposed Metrics names: redwood_degradation_score{route,region,instance}, redwood_score_contributors{...}
Prefer using the existing health-telemetry pipeline (ENG-31877) for input; if unavailable use local aggregate.
Inter-team: Need coordination with Console for new dashboard tiles (PM: Rae Chen).
Performance: scoring computation must be O(n) per-batch and keep memory footprint low; plan to reuse existing aggregator infra.
